title: Eviction score drift causing tenant memory amplification — investigation and guardrails
creator: Asha Raman
description: Summary: A sustained drift in eviction priority scoring caused certain tenants to retain stale prefix entries leading to gradual heap growth and elevated OOM pressure on a subset of serving hosts. The condition surfaced as elevated memory footprints and intermittent request latencies during a capacity-constrained window. This ticket consolidates the investigation, immediate mitigations, and engineering guardrails to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-12 03:14 UTC — On-call alerted: abnormal memory growth on pool-g1 hosts after a deploy
2025-02-12 03:30 UTC — Autoscaler triggered but nodes are approaching OOM and eviction latency rose
2025-02-12 04:00 UTC — Rollback of recent kernel scheduling change (deploy r1.21.4) to stabilize serving latency
2025-02-12 05:20 UTC — Live debug: observed eviction score decay function producing higher scores for older entries under certain workload skews
2025-02-13 — Root cause hypothesis formed and confirmed with repro harness; began crafting mitigations
root_cause: Eviction priority calculation used a decay coefficient that was sensitive to intermittent write storms. Under mixed write/read patterns, historical entries acquired inflated priority (lower eviction probability) due to a timing bug in score decay logic combined with a namespace aggregation anomaly; this allowed stale prefixes to persist and the slab allocator to fragment, resulting in amplified memory usage for affected tenants.
mitigations: Immediate: Rollback of kernel scheduling change and increase eviction worker parallelism on affected pools
Hotfix: Patch to normalize decay coefficient computation and avoid negative time deltas in score update path (deployed to canary)
Traffic-level: Temporarily tighten per-tenant reservation limits to force earlier eviction under high-memory conditions
Operational: Added a short-term alert for >10% sustained deviation from baseline per-host eviction rate
action_items: (MIG-1) Enforce monotonic timestamping in eviction score updates and add unit/regression tests — owner: Miguel Torres — estimate: 3 — status: In Progress
(MIG-2) Implement a bounded max-score cap and decay floor to prevent runaway persistence — owner: Miguel Torres — estimate: 5 — status: Open
(ENG-3) Improve slab fragmentation telemetry: expose per-tenant slab occupancy and live fragmentation ratio — owner: Priya Desai — estimate: 5 — status: Open
(SRE-4) Add automated remediation: when per-host free-memory < 12% trigger tenant-level admission throttle and eviction aggressor — owner: SRE on-call — estimate: 3 — status: Open
(QA-5) Create workload harness that reproduces mixed write/read skew and validates memory stability across 24h — owner: Jamie Chen — estimate: 8 — status: Open
(DOC-6) Update runbook with triage steps and post-incident checklist for eviction-induced memory growth — owner: Maya Patel — estimate: 2 — status: In Progress
